title: chat-client: use base-client PushSubscription bindings instead of private chat-flavoured ones
description:
Design: docs/design/emailpush.md. Decisions: docs/design/DECISIONS.md.
Note key: E14. Crates: jmap-chat-client. Size: S.

Follow-up. Design: docs/design/emailpush.md §8.

jmap-chat-client has private chat-flavoured PushSubscription/get and /set code. Once jmap-base-client has the generic push_subscription_get/push_subscription_set (with extra_using), reimplement the chat-client helpers as thin wrappers over them, keeping the public chat-client API unchanged (or #[deprecated] wrappers per the repo stability policy if a signature must change).
Acceptance: existing chat-client tests pass; no duplicate request-building code remains; public-api snapshot shows no unintended change.
notes: 2026-11-19 (blocked on a decision for Mark): base-client push_subscription_get/set landed (r44n.9). The chat-client helpers cannot become thin wrappers without public API changes: (1) push_subscription_create/update/destroy take if_in_state, but RFC 8620 §7.2.2 says PushSubscription/set 'does *not* take an ifInState argument' — the base binding has none; (2) push_subscription_update/destroy return SetResponse<PartialObject>, whose accountId and newState are required, while §7.2.2 says the response has no accountId/oldState/newState, so a compliant server's response may fail to decode; the base binding returns PushSubscriptionSetResponse. Options: deprecate the if_in_state parameters and the SetResponse returns (new methods returning PushSubscriptionSetResponse), or keep the chat API and only share request building.
